title: Hierarchy: parents and children
cards/0/body:
Any object can be a parent: earth.add(moon). A child's position is measured from its parent: a Moon at x = 1.2 is 1.2 from the Earth, not from the center of the world.

Move, rotate or scale the parent, and the children go along with it.
cards/1/body: THREE.Group is an invisible holder object. Take a solar system: the Earth sits inside a "pivot" group, 4 units from the center. Rotate the pivot and the Earth travels along its orbit.
cards/2/task: The Moon should travel with the Earth. Pick the right parent for it and take two orbit steps.
cards/3/q: Why did the Moon stay put with scene.add(moon)?
cards/3/options/0: Its parent is the scene, and the scene does not rotate; the Earth's pivot has nothing to do with it
cards/3/explain: Motion is passed only down the chain from parent to children.
cards/4/task: Make the Earth twice as big and take one orbit step. What happened to the Moon?
cards/5/q: Why did the Moon move out to 2.4 and grow too?
cards/5/options/0: A parent's scale applies to everything inside it: both the size and the position of its children
cards/5/explain: To grow only the Earth, scale it in a separate group with no children.
cards/6/body: moon.position is the local position relative to the parent. To get the world position, ask like this:
cards/6/code:
const p = new THREE.Vector3();
moon.getWorldPosition(p);   // coordinates in the world
cards/8/q: What does a child inherit from its parent? Select all that apply.
cards/8/explain: Each Mesh has its own material.
